records.issuer: Saudi Data & AI Authority / National Data Management Office
records.title: Personal Data Protection Law
verifiedFacts: The PDPL came into force on 14 September 2023.
The original one-year corrective period targeted compliance by 14 September 2024.
Personal Data includes information that directly or indirectly identifies an individual.

records.issuer: Saudi Data & AI Authority / National Data Management Office
records.title: The Implementing Regulation of the Personal Data Protection Law
verifiedFacts: The Implementing Regulation comes into force from the date of the Law enforcement.

Before or when collecting Personal Data directly, the Controller must provide identity/contact details, applicable DPO contact, legal basis and explicit purpose, retention information, and Data Subject rights information.
Processor selection requires sufficient guarantees and a processing agreement covering purpose, data categories, duration, breach notification and subprocessors.

A documented impact assessment is required in specified higher-risk processing cases including Sensitive Data, dataset linking, certain large-scale/monitoring/new-technology or automated-decision processing, and services likely to cause serious privacy harm.
A qualifying Personal Data Breach must be notified to the Competent Authority within no more than 72 hours after awareness.
DPO appointment is required in specified cases including certain large-scale public processing, systematic monitoring, or core Sensitive Data processing.
Records of Personal Data Processing activities must be maintained during processing and up to five years after the end of a processing activity.

records.issuer: Saudi Data & AI Authority / National Data Management Office
records.title: Regulation on Personal Data Transfer Outside the Kingdom
verifiedFacts: Appropriate safeguards may include approved Binding Common Rules, Standard Contractual Clauses, authorized compliance certifications, or approved binding codes of conduct where applicable.
Risk assessment is required for transfers under specified safeguard/exemption cases and for continuous or large-scale transfer of Sensitive Data.
Risk assessment includes purpose/legal basis, transfer nature/geographic scope, safeguards, data minimization, impact and mitigation measures.

records.title: Implementing Regulation of the Accredited Valuers Law
verifiedFacts: TAQEEM's current rules portal lists the Implementing Regulation of the Accredited Valuers Law.

The regulation defines the professional framework as including the Law, Implementing Regulation, Code of Conduct, adopted valuation standards, professional manuals, continuing education rules, and Authority decisions/instructions.

records.title: Code of Conduct and Ethics of the Valuation Profession
verifiedFacts: The current code was approved by TAQEEM's Board on 24 July 2023.
The rules apply to accredited valuers, Authority members and workers in the profession as applicable.
The code requires professional conduct, confidentiality and compliance with valuation rules and regulations.

records.title: Rules Regulating Real Estate Valuation Services for Financing Entities
verifiedFacts: The rules regulate real estate valuation services for financing entities.
They reference the Implementing Regulation issued by Minister of Finance decision No. 107 dated 28/1/1445H and its amendments.
Financing entities include commercial banks and finance companies licensed and supervised by the Saudi Central Bank.
The rules define Qaym as the unified electronic platform for real estate valuation services supervised by TAQEEM.

records.title: Real Estate Valuation Sector - Professional Obligations
verifiedFacts: TAQEEM states valuation license holders must practice in accordance with the rules regulating the valuation profession.
Valuation reports must be signed by authorized participants in accordance with the Law and related requirements.

TAQEEM states reports are issued in Arabic, with another language permissible by agreement while an Arabic certified copy must be available to the Authority or competent official authority upon request.

A complete work file is required for each final valuation report including correspondence, documents, data, inspections, sources, methods, analysis, calculations and actions supporting the valuation conclusion.

records.title: Approved report template containing minimum requirements
verifiedFacts: TAQEEM's professional-practice digital library currently lists an approved report template containing minimum requirements for real-estate valuation reports and other valuation sectors.

remainingExternalReview: Saudi counsel/professional reviewer must determine which TAQEEM/REGA provisions legally apply to STARTAK's actual operating model, users, report outputs and commercial launch model.

PDPL counsel/privacy officer must validate controller/processor roles, data inventory, lawful bases, notices, retention, Data Subject rights, DPIA triggers, breach workflow, subprocessors and international transfers against actual architecture and contracts.
Current TAQEEM minimum-report template must be fetched and mapped section-by-section before formal Taqeem report-conformance claims.
Financing-purpose deployment requires separate Qaym/SAMA operational and legal review.
No production control is considered implemented merely because its official legal source is recorded here.
